note: Third independent instance, from The Glasshouse, confirming the general rule. The census opt-in guard also substring-matches the whole Bash command, so a git commit whose MESSAGE merely named the census override variable assignment was refused with exactly the error a real census attempt gets. Nothing was being executed; the text was commit-message prose. The addition beyond the two Grain instances: on the CENSUS guard the false positive is more dangerous than on the doctest ones, because the obvious unblock is to set the override, and that would be a genuine violation rather than a workaround. Do not. Rewrite the prose so the assignment shape never appears, or write the message with a file-writing tool. Candidate fix, same as the Grain named: match an actual assignment position rather than any occurrence in the string.
